text: A pendulum clock's escapement turns repeated swings into small advances of a toothed wheel, allowing the mechanism to count an oscillator's cycles.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NIST, Everyday Time and Atomic Time, Part 3; https://www.nist.gov/blogs/taking-measure/everyday-time-and-atomic-time-part-3. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: A clock escapement gives a pendulum small pushes to replace energy lost during its motion. Counting swings and sustaining them are coupled tasks.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NIST, A Walk Through Time; https://tf.nist.gov/general/pdf/1796.pdf. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: An underdamped oscillator crosses equilibrium repeatedly as its motion fades.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 15.5; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/15-5-damped-oscillations. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: In an ideal linear spring-and-mass system, critical damping returns the mass to equilibrium as quickly as possible without oscillation.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 15.5; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/15-5-damped-oscillations. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: More damping is not always faster: an overdamped spring-and-mass system returns without oscillating but more slowly than a critically damped one.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 15.5; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/15-5-damped-oscillations. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: A viscous damping model makes the resisting force proportional to velocity and opposite to motion, removing mechanical energy.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 15.5; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/15-5-damped-oscillations. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: Small repeated pushes can produce a large motion when their timing matches an oscillator's resonant response.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 15.6; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/15-6-forced-oscillations. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.

text: Lightly damped oscillators respond strongly over a narrower band of driving frequencies. Heavier damping broadens and reduces the response.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 15.6; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/15-6-forced-oscillations. Consulted 2026-10-13. OpenStax educational text is CC BY 4.0; this record is independently worded.
